catalyst_text: Presented positive late-breaking Phase 3 and real-world data
detailed_catalyst_text: New late-breaking and real-world data in primary biliary cholangitis were presented at EASL, including a post hoc Phase 3 analysis showing clinically meaningful fatigue improvements versus placebo in patients with moderate-to-severe baseline fatigue. A U.S. real-world cohort with ALP 1–1.67 x ULN showed significant ALP reductions with 59% achieving normalization by 6 months, and a Phase IV interim analysis showed rapid biochemical and symptom improvements with favorable tolerability. These findings strengthen evidence for both disease control and symptom relief in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: PARIS, FRANCE, 2026-05-28 - Ipsen (Euronext: IPN, OTC:IPSEY) today announced the presentation of new late-breaking results from the ELATIVE Phase III trial and two real-world studies at the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) congress. In a post hoc analysis of the pivotal ELATIVE study, shared in a late-breaking presentation, patients with moderate-to-severe fatigue at baseline experienced greater fatigue reductions with IQIRVO compared to placebo across 52 weeks. A clinically meaningful improvement in fatigue was achieved in 67% of patients on IQIRVO vs 31% on placebo (p=0.020) at Week 52, with improvements observed as early as Week 4. These data showed that improvements were observed through to month 6 in patients who were naïve to second-line treatment with 72% of patients having a ≥15% ALP reduction, a decline in mean ALP from 174 U/L to 131 U/L and 59% of patients achieving ALP normalization. In a third late-breaker, interim month 3 findings from the global Phase IV ELFINITY study, conducted in routine clinical practice, showed IQIRVO delivered rapid and sustained reductions in ALP for three months, with biochemical response achieved in 55% of patients. More than half of patients with baseline moderate-to-severe fatigue experienced clinically meaningful improvements by month 3 as well as clinically important improvements in pruritus. IQIRVO demonstrated a favorable tolerability profile consistent with previous studies, with no serious or severe treatment-emergent adverse events reported.

catalyst_text: Announced positive head to head Phase IV results
detailed_catalyst_text: Results from the Phase IV DIRECTION head-to-head trial in adults with upper limb spasticity showed non-inferior safety versus onabotulinumtoxinA and a longer duration of effect. The randomized, double-blind crossover study observed a 20.3% vs 23.0% TEAE rate and 14.2 vs 13.8 weeks duration, reinforcing durable symptom control in this setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: PARIS, FRANCE – 2026-05-19 – Ipsen ((Euronext: IPN, OTC:IPSEY) announced today results from the only prospective, head-to-head Phase IV DIRECTION trial comparing Dysport® (abobotulinumtoxinA) to Botox® (onabotulinumtoxinA) in adults living with upper limb spasticity (ULS)1. The trial showed that patients treated with Dysport had a non-inferior safety profile to Botox and achieved longer-lasting symptom control (based on a pre-specified 80% confidence interval)1. For the primary endpoint of the trial, Dysport demonstrated non-inferiority compared with Botox with a treatment-emergent adverse event rate of 20.3% vs 23.0%, respectively (adjusted difference (aboBoNT-A – onaBoNT-A) was −2.7% (80%CI: −6.2%, 0.9%)1. In addition, the secondary efficacy endpoint was met: patients treated with Dysport experienced a longer duration of effect compared with those treated with Botox (14.2 vs 13.8 weeks, respectively; adjusted difference favoring Dysport (80%CI: 0.2, 5.9) with a pre-specified significance threshold for statistical significance (p=0.17; significance threshold, p=0.20).

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 2 data at conference
detailed_catalyst_text: New Phase II results were presented for glabellar lines from the LANTIC trial, including Step 3 proof-of-concept (n=183). The study met the primary endpoint with 66% achieving a ≥2-grade improvement vs 0% placebo at Week 4 and showed sustained benefit at Week 24 vs placebo and Dysport, alongside high patient satisfaction.
catalyst_text_evidence: PARIS, FRANCE, 2026-05-16 – Ipsen (Euronext: IPN, OTC:IPSEY) today presented the first corabotase data (n=183) for moderate-to- severe glabellar lines at the 2026 Scale Symposium in Nashville, TN. In the trial, at Week 4, 66% of patients treated with corabotase (50ng) showed a statistically significant ≥2-grade improvement (composite response) vs 0% with placebo, p=0.0001 (primary endpoint). At Week 24, 60.8% of patients treated with corabotase (50ng) experienced clinically significant sustained duration of effect vs placebo (0.2%) and vs Dysport (36.7%), defined as an investigator-assessed score of "none" or "mild" of line severity. These results were reinforced by patient satisfaction scores with 82.8% of those treated with corabotase (50ng) rating "very satisfied" or "satisfied" on the Subject Level of Satisfaction (SLS) 4-point categorical scale.

drug_indication: Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma with BRAF alteration
catalyst_text: Received EU conditional approval for pediatric brain tumors
detailed_catalyst_text: The European Commission granted conditional marketing authorization for tovorafenib monotherapy for patients 6 months and older with pediatric low-grade glioma harboring BRAF fusion or rearrangement, or BRAF V600 mutation after progression on prior systemic therapy. The decision applies to all 27 EU Member States plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. This provides a new targeted option for relapsed or refractory BRAF-altered pLGG across Europe.
catalyst_text_evidence: the European Commission (EC) has granted conditional marketing authorization for Ojemda (tovorafenib) as monotherapy for the treatment of patients 6 months of age and older with pediatric low-grade-glioma harboring a BRAF fusion or rearrangement, or BRAF V600 mutation, who have progressed after one or more prior systemic therapies. This EC decision applies across all 27 EU Member States, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway.

catalyst_text: Announced withdrawal due to unfavorable safety concerns
detailed_catalyst_text: Therapy was voluntarily withdrawn from all marketed indications, including follicular lymphoma and epithelioid sarcoma. The decision followed IDMC advice from the Phase Ib/III SYMPHONY-1 trial citing secondary hematologic malignancies, and all active studies and expanded access programs were halted.
catalyst_text_evidence: PARIS, FRANCE, 2026-03-09 – Ipsen announced today that it is voluntarily withdrawing Tazverik® (tazemetostat) in all indications from all Ipsen markets. As a result of these data, Ipsen is withdrawing Tazverik effective immediately, including both for follicular lymphoma (FL) and epithelioid sarcoma (ES). In addition to withdrawing Tazverik from the market, Ipsen has initiated steps to stop treatment with tazemetostat for all patients currently enrolled in the ongoing SYMPHONY-1 trial. Ipsen is also discontinuing all active tazemetostat clinical trials and expanded access programs.

catalyst_text: Pivotal Phase 2 trial reported negative topline results
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline results from a pivotal Phase II study in adults and children with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva showed the primary endpoint was not met versus placebo. The study is being closed as a result; the therapy was generally well tolerated with no safety concerns reported. This outcome informs future research directions in this ultra-rare condition.
catalyst_text_evidence: "Ipsen today announced that the pivotal Phase II FALKON trial did not meet its primary endpoint of reducing new heterotopic ossification (HO) in adults and children living with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) vs. placebo, as a result the study will be closed." "The investigational medicinal product (fidrisertib) was generally well tolerated, with no safety concerns in the trial."
